name: Procurement and Government Benefit Fraud
description: Fraud against public bodies and large buyers includes bid rigging, inflated invoices, fictitious suppliers and false benefit claims. Collusion between suppliers and officials is a recurring pattern.

sources.text: OECD, Guidelines for Fighting Bid Rigging in Public Procurement (2009, rev. 2025)
UK Government Counter Fraud Function, Public Sector Fraud Authority publications
ACFE, Occupational Fraud 2024: A Report to the Nations (2024)

exposure.rationale: Fraud against public bodies and large buyers via bid rigging, fictitious suppliers and false benefit claims; officials collude with suppliers; payments flow through procurement/purchasing.

indicators.name: Tenders show suspiciously similar pricing or documents
indicators.canon: Tenders show suspiciously similar pricing or documents
indicators.desc: Bids contain shared errors, formatting or pricing relationships.
indicators.ctx: Bids contain shared errors, formatting or pricing relationships.
refs: OECD, guidelines for fighting bid rigging in public procurement (general)

indicators.name: Rotation of winning bidders
indicators.desc: Contracts win in turn across a small group.
indicators.ctx: Contracts win in turn across a small group.
refs: OECD, guidelines for fighting bid rigging in public procurement (general)

indicators.name: Contract splitting to avoid thresholds
indicators.canon: Payments or claims split to stay below internal approval limits
indicators.desc: Payments, claims or contracts are broken into amounts just under internal authorisation limits.
indicators.ctx: Series of awards just below tender limits.
refs: OECD, guidelines for fighting bid rigging in public procurement (general)

indicators.name: Supplier is shell company with no footprint
indicators.canon: Shell entity with no operating footprint
indicators.desc: Entity has no staff, premises, website or trading history consistent with its stated activity, yet receives significant payments.
indicators.ctx: Registered address and staff do not match the supply.
refs: OECD, guidelines for fighting bid rigging in public procurement (general)

indicators.name: Invoices for services or goods not received
indicators.canon: Invoices for services or goods not received
indicators.desc: Payment is approved without delivery evidence.
indicators.ctx: Payment is approved without delivery evidence.
refs: OECD, guidelines for fighting bid rigging in public procurement (general)

indicators.name: Official has undisclosed relationship with supplier
indicators.canon: Official has undisclosed relationship with supplier
indicators.desc: Conflict of interest appears from registry or declarations.
indicators.ctx: Conflict of interest appears from registry or declarations.
refs: OECD, guidelines for fighting bid rigging in public procurement (general)

indicators.name: Benefit claimants share bank accounts or addresses
indicators.canon: Multiple customers sharing contact details or addresses
indicators.desc: Unrelated customers or applicants share the same phone, email, address, device or bank account, including mail drops and shared accommodation.
indicators.ctx: Many claims route to same accounts or addresses.
refs: OECD, guidelines for fighting bid rigging in public procurement (general)

indicators.name: Claim details contradict income or residency evidence
indicators.canon: Claim details inconsistent with income, residency or account history
indicators.desc: Declared income, dependants or circumstances conflict with data held on the customer.
refs: OECD, guidelines for fighting bid rigging in public procurement (general)

indicators.name: Spike in claims via one agent or channel
indicators.canon: Spike in volume via a single channel, agent or source
indicators.desc: Unusual surge in accounts or claims originating from one channel, introducer, agent, IP range or device.
refs: OECD, guidelines for fighting bid rigging in public procurement (general)
